newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ electricity futures trade for first time.
newsitem.headline: NZ electricity futures trade for first time.

text.p: Electricity futures listed on the New Zealand Futures and Options Exchange recorded their first trades on Friday, two months after making their debut.
The March 1997 contract traded at NZ$45.9/megawatt hour and the April 1997 contract at $46.8/Mwhr.
The contracts are aimed at controlling risk associated with volatility in the spot electricity price on New Zealand's wholesale electricity market.

NZFOE Chief Executive Peter Mansell said he expected more power companies, generators and industrial and corporate electricity users to actively use futures as the market developed to protect against adverse spot movements.
